sections.presenting_complaint: Increased exertional breathlessness and palpitations for 3 weeks, on a background of atrial fibrillation diagnosed 18 months ago.
sections.history: Breathless on stairs, palpitations. No chest pain. Occasional postural light-headedness; no syncope. Mild evening ankle swelling. No orthopnoea. Single episode of fresh red rectal bleeding three weeks ago, not previously reported; no recurrence, no melaena, no change in bowel habit or weight loss. Attended with daughter, who manages her dosette box.
sections.medications_allergies: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily (initially reported as once daily; daughter confirmed twice daily). Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily. Levothyroxine 75 micrograms once daily. Codeine intolerance (nausea).
sections.examination: Pulse irregularly irregular, rate 104. BP 128/76. Heart sounds irregular, no murmur. Fine bibasal crackles. Mild bilateral ankle oedema. Weight 58 kg. ECG: atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate approximately 105. Bloods: creatinine 98, thyroid function normal.
sections.impression: Atrial fibrillation with suboptimal rate control, likely contributing to breathlessness; possible early heart failure. Apixaban dose appropriate (age 72, weight 58 kg, creatinine 98). Single episode of rectal bleeding on anticoagulation requiring investigation.
sections.plan: Increase bisoprolol to 5 mg once daily. Echocardiogram within 6 weeks. Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily; do not stop. Letter to GP: FBC, FIT, and consider lower GI referral. Clinic review in 3 months after echocardiogram.
sections.safety_netting: Attend A&E if further significant bleeding, black stools or feeling faint. Call 999 if breathing worsens significantly, especially lying flat, or chest pain.
